sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries — list direct reports; department: filtering employees by department; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filtering active policies for assignment and balance calculation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for an employee; status: filter by status (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED); leave_policy_id: filter requests by leave type/policy; start_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager approval history queries

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up all balances for an employee; leave_policy_id: look up balances by policy; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique composite lookup for balance enforcement during leave application

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up all audit records for a specific entity; performed_by: audit trail by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filter audit records by action type

methods: findByEmployeeId(employeeId: string, params: LeaveRequestQueryParams): Promise<{ rows: LeaveRequest[]; total: number }>
findByApproverId(managerId: string, params: LeaveRequestQueryParams): Promise<{ rows: LeaveRequest[]; total: number }>
updateStatus(id: string, status: LeaveStatus, approvedBy?: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>
findOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date, excludeId?: string): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId: string, leavePolicyId: string, fiscalYear: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
updateUsedDays(id: string, usedDays: number, remainingDays: number): Promise<LeaveBalance>
updateEntitlement(id: string, totalEntitlement: number, remainingDays: number): Promise<LeaveBalance>
findByActor(performedBy: string, limit?: number, offset?: number): Promise<{ rows: AuditLog[]; total: number }>

data_notes: All five tables defined conceptually: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. Five repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool. The leave_requests table references leave_policies (not a separate leave_types table) since the DOMAIN.md defines LeaveType as an enum on LeavePolicy.leave_type. The audit_logs table satisfies GP-002 — every state-changing operation writes here. All repositories follow the module naming convention: src/modules/{module}/{module}.repository.ts.
